title: Container Security
summary: A practical threat model for containers and the controls that matter: non-root users, dropped capabilities, no-new-privileges, read-only filesystems, seccomp/AppArmor, rootless Docker, secret handling, image scanning, SBOMs, signing and patching.
objectives: Explain the container threat model and why a container is not a security boundary by default
Run containers with least privilege: non-root, `--cap-drop ALL`, `no-new-privileges`, read-only root filesystem with tmpfs
Describe what the default seccomp and AppArmor profiles do and when user namespaces or rootless Docker help
Handle secrets correctly at build time (BuildKit secrets) and runtime (files, not ENV or layers)
Scan images with Docker Scout, Trivy or Grype, generate SBOMs and provenance, and sign/verify images with cosign
Choose minimal base images, keep them patched, and audit a host with docker-bench-security
